titleText.es: Creo que el IETF alzancó un equilibrio perfecto con lo de los 128 bits. Podemos meter las direcciones MAC en una subred /64, y los nanobots solo podrán devorar medio planeta.
titleText.en: I think the IETF hit the right balance with the 128 bits thing. We can fit MAC addresses in a /64 subnet, and the nanobots will only be able to devour half the planet.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish title attribute is preserved exactly, including its printed typo alzancó. Spanish OCR corrections restore QUÉ twice, DIRECCIONES, DEBERÍAMOS, MICRAS, CÚBICAS, the punctuation around ¿POR?, and the opening exclamation mark before SE. The percentage, year, and IPv6 label are audited non-lexical exclusions.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A comandante is the person in charge of a military unit or operation.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; marks detenerse, “to stop”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With a form of detener, se shows that the people or things themselves come to a stop.
After a form of haber, detenido is detenerse’s completed-action form here.
After a form of haber, parado presents the stopping as completed.
Quietos is masculine plural because it describes more than one nanobot.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins a menos que, “unless”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A is fixed as the first part of the connector a menos que.

example.en: I will go unless it rains.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; middle of a menos que, “unless”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Menos is fixed between a and que in this connector.

example.en: We are leaving unless it snows.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; completes a menos que, “unless”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Que completes the connector and introduces the possible exception.

example.es: Ven, a menos que estés ocupado.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here volumen means how much physical space an object occupies, not sound level.

example.es: Calculamos el volumen de la caja.
example.en: We calculated the volume of the box.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A micra is the everyday Spanish name for a micrometre, one millionth of a metre.
Cúbicas is feminine plural to match micras.

example.es: La muestra ocupa cinco micras cúbicas.
example.en: The sample occupies five cubic micrometres.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: why?; for what reason? (with qué left understood)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In the short echo ¿por?, the usual qué is omitted because the question being repeated is already clear.
Here hecho is the completed-action form of hacer in the pattern that makes someone do something.

example.es: La broma nos ha hecho reír.
example.en: The joke has made us laugh.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: With tiempo, ganar means to obtain extra time before something happens.

example.es: La pausa nos permite ganar tiempo.
example.en: The pause lets us buy time.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: An enjambre is a large moving group, especially of insects or, by extension, tiny robots.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: by; when you say (introducing the wording being explained)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After querer decir, con can introduce the exact word or expression whose meaning is being asked about.
Here agotadas describes a supply of addresses that has all been used, not tired people.
After haber, migrado is migrar’s completed-action form.

example.es: La empresa ha migrado al sistema nuevo.
example.en: The company has migrated to the new system.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you introduce a possible exception that would change what you just said?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A menos que introduces a possible exception. The verb after it normally uses a special form because the exception is not presented as a fact; for example, llueve changes to llueva.

example.en: We will go unless it rains.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: hacer + persona + verbo en forma de diccionario
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that someone or something makes a person do an action?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a matching form of hacer, then the affected person, then the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The unchanged dictionary form ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Only hacer changes for the person and time. A short word such as me, te, or nos usually marks who is made to act; in a compound form such as ha hecho, that short word comes before the helper ha.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “to gain time” or “to buy time”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: to gain time; to buy time
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ganar literally means to win or gain. With tiempo it conventionally means creating or obtaining extra time before a deadline or event.

example.es: Haz una pregunta para ganar tiempo.
example.en: Ask a question to buy time.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: IPv6’s original specification appeared in 1998; the joke treats an IPv6 address block as the finite supply of identities available to a nanobot swarm.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The core IPv6 specification, RFC 2460, was published in 1998. IPv4’s limited address space motivated IPv6, whose 128-bit addresses are unimaginably numerous. The comic imagines self-replicating nanobots stopping after consuming only part of Earth because their swarm was still assigned too small an IPv6 subnet and ran out of addresses.
